text: Three seventeen am, it smelled of yeast and silence. Marisol slid the first loaves into the oven. Then, there it was: the worn paperback of The Borrowers, in the wicker basket by the back door. Every Thursday, for six weeks, someone has left it here instead of the library two blocks over. No name, no card. Just the book. Smelled of rain and woodsmoke. Tonight there was a folded note between pages 84 and 85. She wiped her floury hands and opened it. It said: I can't make it to the library before closing. Please keep it another week. I like knowing it's warm. Marisol looked at the basket, then at the tray of cinnamon rolls cooling on the rack. Picked the one with the most icing. Wrapped it in wax paper, put the note back in the book, set both by the door. Then flipped the sign to OPEN and started the coffee.
